items.followUp: State two functions of bile in digestion.

rubric.why: Emulsification breaks large fat globules into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area available to lipase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that bile emulsifies fats or breaks them into small droplets.

rubric.why: Bile helps neutralize the acidic food entering the small intestine from the stomach, making conditions suitable for digestive enzymes.
rubric.description: Bile neutralizes acidic chyme or provides an alkaline medium.

modelAnswer: Bile salts emulsify fats into small droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase.
Bile also neutralizes acidic chyme from the stomach and provides an alkaline medium in the small intestine.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and two functions of the nucleus.

accept: controls the activities of the cell
rubric.why: The nucleus acts as the control centre of the cell.
rubric.description: States that the nucleus controls cell activities.

rubric.why: Chromosomes in the nucleus carry hereditary information.
rubric.description: Identifies hereditary material in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus contains hereditary information or genetic material in chromosomes.

rubric.why: The nucleus is enclosed by a double membrane, which has pores.
rubric.description: Describes the nuclear envelope and its pores.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the double nuclear membrane and pores.

rubric.why: The diagram should clearly show a recognizable nucleus enclosed by its membrane.
rubric.description: Draws a recognizable nucleus with its membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clearly drawn nucleus with a surrounding membrane.

rubric.why: These are the main internal structures shown in the nucleus diagram.
rubric.description: Shows and labels the internal structures of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing and labelling nucleoplasm, chromatin and nucleolus.

modelAnswer: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell and contains hereditary information in the form of chromosomes.
It is surrounded by a double nuclear membrane with pores; its interior contains nucleoplasm, chromatin and a nucleolus.
Diagram construction: Draw an outer circle 6 cm in diameter and a second circle 0.3 cm inside it to show the double nuclear membrane.
Draw several small openings through both circles to represent nuclear pores; draw thread-like chromatin and one small circle for the nucleolus inside the nucleus.
Label the diagram: nuclear membrane, nuclear pore, nucleoplasm, chromatin and nucleolus.
